case.case_title: Palitha v. O.I.C., Police Station, Polonnaruwa and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 880/92, decided on 4 May 1993

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s detention without proper rehabilitation and misinformation to the Court violated his rights under Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that he was detained unlawfully without being sent for rehabilitation as previously stated to the Court, thus infringing his fundamental rights under Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents initially provided incorrect information that the petitioner was due to be released after rehabilitation, which was later corrected to confirm continued detention.
key_facts: Petitioner detained since 08.11.1989 at Pelawatta Detention Camp.
Court was misinformed that petitioner was released on 30.04.1992 due to typographical error.
Petitioner was not sent for rehabilitation despite earlier communication.
Petitioner was released on 30.04.1993 directly from detention.
Respondents did not file any objection to the application.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 13(2) as protecting detainees from being held without a legal order and requiring that any detention be properly authorized and communicated to the Court.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner was detained without proper rehabilitation and the Court was misled by incorrect information, the Court found an infringement of Article 13(2) rights.
principles_established: Courts have inherent power to set aside orders made on wrong facts to remedy injustice.
Detention without proper legal process or misinformation to the Court violates Article 13(2).
precedents_cited: Wijeyesinghe v. Uluwita 34 NLR p. 362 at p. 364
Ganeshanathan v. Goonewardena [1984] 1 Sri LR p. 319 at p. 329

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner’s rights under Article 13(2) were infringed and set aside the previous dismissal order.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of infringement of rights and payment of Rs. 17,500 as compensation to the petitioner.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central because the petitioner’s detention without proper legal order and misinformation to the Court directly violated the protections guaranteed by this clause.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court found that the petitioner was still in detention despite being informed otherwise, and that the order was made on wrong facts to the petitioner’s prejudice.
